Le Bris has been given a stay of execution – will he take advantage of it? We’ll soon find out. Goalkeeper: Robin Roefs Roefs can’t be happy at present playing in front of a team that’s continually leaving him exposed – he’s produced some great saves in recent European games and hopefully he has a good night tonight. top.title: New CBA proposal adjusts salary cap, floor
top.description: ATLANTA, GA - MAY 13: A locked padlock and chain against two official MLB baseballs representing a potential lockout between Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) for the 2027 MLB season, as photographed on May 13, 2026 in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Major League Baseball has amended its salary cap and floor proposal to the MLB Players Association. Now that the 2026 season is complete and baseball is into its offseason, MLB has proposed delaying the start of the salary cap and floor to the 2028 season. The rest of their proposals would begin with the 2027 season but the teams would have a full season to make adjustments to prepare themselves for the coming changes. The owners further proposed increasing the cap to $258.2 million from the original $245.3 million and the floor to $180.2 million from $171.2 million. The new numbers reflect a 50-50 split of the projected revenue for the 2028 season. A change to the retirement proposal The offer also includes $282 million in luxury tax revenue to be given to players in cash payments instead of being placed into retirement benefits. In the present system, when a team pays luxury tax, half of the money goes into player benefits and the other half to the teams. For the 2027 season, the league is offering to pay the retirement portion directly to the players. According to league estimates , $285,000 would go to each player who received a full year of service time, $213,400 to a player with three-quarters of a year of service, $142,300 to a player with a half year of service, and $71,100 to any player with a quarter year of service. Teams outside the guidelines Per the MLB numbers, 12 teams would have to raise payroll to meet the minimum proposed floor while eight teams would have to decrease their payroll to meet the cap. Those numbers are based on current payrolls and would change based on what teams spend in 2027. Players response The MLB Players Association predictably responded negatively to the new offer. “MLB owners continue to propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values.” The statement continued, “a massive reduction in player compensation, elimination of fundamental player rights, plus a gutting of domestic and international amateur entry systems.” A statement virtually identical to the previous proposal from the owners. Sweetening the pot? This appears to be an attempt by the league to sweeten the deal for the players but doesn’t seem to have the desired effect. The baseline for the union is their unwillingness to accept a salary cap and floor as the start of negotiations. The current contract expires and 11:59 pm eastern time on Dec. 1. The owners have made it clear they intend to lock the players out if no deal is reached by that time.

top.description: ZAGREB, CROATIA - OCTOBER 22: Iker Almena of GNK Dinamo Zagreb and Luka Ivanusec of GNK Dinamo Zagreb during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between GNK Dinamo and N.E.C. (Photo by Josip Regovic/Pixsell/MB Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dinamo won both the Croatian league and cup last season under Mario Kovačević. How would you reflect on that campaign and what were the expectations among supporters heading into this season? Last season’s campaign went about as well as Dinamo wanted after not winning anything the season prior; they dominated and returned to their usual form. They always want to win the domestic double; they essentially take it for granted. So the real challenges/expectations come in Europe, with them being back in the UCL qualifiers; the club and the fans want to return to the UCL. This didn’t happen, as they lost to the Norwegian side, Viking, because of their poor defensive lapses in concentration, as they conceded two goals in quick succession in both legs. This left the fans mad at the higher-ups for not bringing in immediate improvements for the squad beforehand, and at the coach for the poor reactions from the team. Dinamo currently sit second behind Hajduk in the league and Saturday’s shock 1-0 defeat to Rudeš ultimately proved to be Mario Kovačević’s final match. What has gone wrong in recent weeks? It’s just the players’ form; everybody except Dion Drena Beljo is struggling to play at a good level game after game. The defence, especially, has been the most inconsistent. Consistently losing their man or having poor reactions inside the box. Kovačević has tried to tweak a few things, with some changes to the starting XIs here and there, but nothing has clicked. Even if a player performed well in one match, the next, he doesn’t. Kovačević left the club by mutual consent just four days before the trip to Sunderland despite winning the double last season. Were you surprised by that decision and do you think it was the right one? Not surprised by the decision at all; it was a long time coming, as in September fans were already calling for his departure after really poor performances vs. Istra, Osijek and Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Even in victories, Dinamo were unconvincing and barely got them over the line, as they were put under serious pressure by Gorica and Lokomotiv, for example. I think it’s the right decision, because at the end of the day, Kovačević has struggled a LOT and hasn’t delivered after saying time and time again, “We need to improve next match,” and that never happened. It seems like the pressure of a bad slump really got to him, since it’s the first one he’s had that is this bad. top.description: Patsy Gallacher, Sunderland (Photo by Barratts/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images While 1937 is rightly remembered for Sunderland’s first FA Cup win, in league terms the season hadn’t been a success – at least compared to the previous campaign. After claiming the title in 1936, the lads finished the 36/37 season in eighth place – 13 points behind winners Manchester City – and finished in the same position the following season, albeit just eight points shy of champions Arsenal. The FA Cup had once again been in tantalising grasp – only for Huddersfield Town to snatch the potential of the holders retaining the trophy with a semi-final defeat. 1938/39 began with a renewed determination to reclaim the title – or at least seriously compete for it – but on this day in 1938, Sunderland finally won their first home game of the season on their sixth attempt – climbing to 6th position in the top flight in the process. Unbeknown to anyone watching on that day, it would be the highest we’d rank in the table for eight years – and it signalled the end of an era for this talented Sunderland team. The 38/39 season saw us finish 16th, only six points off a relegation spot, after a run of just 5 wins in the season’s remaining 22 games saw us drift down the table, and the following season was curtailed due to the outbreak of WW2. But on this day back in 1938, things seemed a lot brighter as the final whistle went. A Sunderland team featuring eight of the 11 who’d played at Wembley 18 months earlier had comprehensively beaten Stoke City 3-0, turning in an excellent performance that saw Patsy Gallacher net his 100th goal in league football. He’d been on 99 since scoring away at Grimsby in March – and typically went on to score his 101st just eight minutes later. Or did he? We’ll get back to that momentarily. top.title: An Introduction to Dinamo Zagreb: What Can Sunderland Expect?
top.description: On the occasion of the International tie Day at Saint Mark's square in front of Saint Mark church on upper town, Honour Cravat Regiment changing the guard on 18 Oct 2014, Zagreb,Croatia. (Photo by Alen Gurovic/NurPhoto) (Photo by NurPhoto/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Tonight, Sunderland play their second Europa League home game of the campaign, as the Lads welcome Dinamo Zagreb to Wearside. Here’s what you need to know about the Croatian champions! Zagreb: Croatia’s Capital With a population of around 750,000, Zagreb is Croatia’s largest city, and the use of its name dates back nearly 1000 years to 1094 AD. The city emerged from two medieval settlements (Gric and Kaptol) and began rapid development and expansion when the two combined in the 19th century. It has played a crucial role in the political history of Croatia, and in 1941 it became the capital of a Croatian puppet state controlled by the Axis powers. After being freed in 1945, Croatia became a part of Yugoslavia from the end of the Second World War until 1991. Zagreb was the centre of a newly independent Croatia during and following the Croatian War of Independence (1991-1995). On a lighter note, Zagreb is home to the world’s shortest public transport funicular, which connects the city’s old town to its newer Novi Zagreb area. It spans a total of 66m, and between its opening in 1890 to 1934, it was powered by steam. Nowadays, the journey is electrified and lasts approximately a minute. The city also keeps many of its old traditions. Every day at noon, a cannon is fired from Lotrščak Tower beside the funicular to mark midday. This has happened every day since 1877. Zagreb also has over 200 gas street lamps which are still lit manually every night, and this tradition dates back to 1863. There are also a number of weird and wonderful museums to visit in the Croatian capital. These include the Museum of Hangovers, the Museum of Laughter, the Museum of Broken Relationships, and a mushroom museum. Dinamo Zagreb: A Brief History Dinamo Zagreb were initially formed in 1911 when Croatia was a part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Upon the end of the Second World War, the club was dissolved by communist authorities; however, it was re-established just three days later on the ninth of June, 1945. The new club inherited the colours, nickname, badge and fanbase of the original club. Its name was changed to Croatia Zagreb in 1993 – a move which was seen as a political move to move away from the club’s communist past amidst Croatian independence. However, this name was never accepted by supporters, and the name Dinamo Zagreb was reinstated in the year 2000. Dinamo Zagreb is Croatia’s most successful club and has lifted the Croatian league 25 times, most recently last season, in which they finished 20 points ahead of second-placed Hajduk Split. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve all seen how things have gone wrong over the last few days, weeks and months and a lot of errors could be attributed to Régis Le Bris over that period. It looks like the club are backing Le Bris for at least a little bit longer in the hope that he can figure the whole mess out and get some points on the board. Whether you agree with the decision or not, I’m sure many of you have some opinions on how he should go about changing our fortunes, and I’m no different! So, I thought it would be fun to have a look at some things he may consider to flip the script for the Lads in the coming weeks with the fair caveat that although I think these are fair points to raise, I believe that Le Bris is a truly gifted manager with more knowledge and experience of the game than I could ever hope to possess. For that reason, I’ll be offering some counters to each point for a bit of balance. Pick a style First up for me is to pick a style and to stick to it. To my eyes, it looks like we have no clear sense of direction or intention in our play anymore. When we have the ball, we often pass it from side to side without incision. When we don’t, we sit deeply without any quick players to counter incisively. We’ve seemingly lost our patterns of play, our triangles and a clear way of moving through the thirds dangerously, and it looks like Le Bris is stuck between two styles at the moment. Disregarding his first five or so games in charge wherein he employed a wonderfully intense press in the Championship, he’s has generally and successfully set us up as a defensively solid team that’s clinical in transition. Instead, Vic Schaefer introduced six new players to the crowd of 9,688 fans at Moody Center before a strange season opener that resembled very little of last season's team that fell to eventual national champion UCLA in the Final Four semifinals last April. It would have been seven but freshman forward Brihanna Crittendon suffered an eye injury in Wednesday's shootaround and unavailable for the first game of the year. The growing pains were obvious. And Schaefer made no bones about the need to improve almost overnight after watching his No. 6 Longhorns struggle - relatively speaking by the coach's standards - in an uneven 85-65 win over a solid Fairleigh Dickinson. "We didn't play very well defensively," Schaefer said. "They got off 20 3s on us, and we pride ourselves on pressure and denying shots, and most of them were wide open. They weren't even contested." top.title: Como boss Cesc Fabregas admits he was 'angry' to concede despite breaking Italian away scoring record in 9-1 Champions League win at Lens
top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-LENS-COMO - AFP Como head coach Cesc Fabregas expressed frustration over failing to keep a clean sheet even after watching his side dismantle Lens 9-1 on Wednesday night. No Italian club had previously managed seven away goals in European Cup or Champions League history before the Serie A visitors ran riot in France. Italian visitors rewrite history books Fabregas saw his maiden Champions League away win slightly soured by a second-half consolation strike as Como recorded their sixth consecutive victory across all competitions. Having beaten RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home either side of a 3-2 loss at Feyenoord, the visitors climbed to fourth in the standings despite missing Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao, Jesus Rodriguez and Jayden Addai. Tournament top scorer Tasos Douvikas netted a treble to score in all four European outings, while Nico Paz, Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and 18-year-old debutant Matteo Papaccioli also struck. Manager urges humility after rout Speaking to Sky Sport Italia about sitting fourth midway through the league phase, Fabregas smiled: "It is also our fourth ever Champions League game, so four is the key number here. "I'm happy, this is football and everything went our way. The lads did well, now we have to prepare for a very important match on Sunday, the ninth in a run between breaks for international duty." Urging his young squad to stay grounded after their historic display, the Spaniard added: "It is a wonderful night for Como, for all our fans and many lads here who are at the start of their careers, but they need to keep their feet on the ground, be humble, keep learning and not think everything will go well from here on. "They must keep working to continue these performances." Defensive lapse frustrates former midfielder Despite almost every goal coming from slick passing moves out from the back and an early penalty against Maxence Caqueret being overturned by VAR, Como are still waiting for their first European shutout after conceding a 65th-minute corner volley. Reflecting on that solitary blemish, Fabregas confessed: "I am angry over the goal we conceded, as we changed something in our defending with the three substitutions. "Plus it was scored by a former teammate of mine, I played with Ruben Aguilar at Monaco, and I told him I'd never seen you score a goal like that before! It was honestly a great goal." Defending champions await this weekend Como must now shift their focus back to domestic duties ahead of a challenging Serie A Matchday 11 trip to reigning Scudetto holders Inter on Sunday , November 8, prior to the international break. On the continental front, the Lariani will resume their league phase campaign by hosting AEK Athens and visiting Real Betis. Fabregas' men will then wrap up their schedule against Paris Saint-Germain before travelling to Barcelona on January 27.

nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THERE are strong indications that the National Assembly is prepared to transmit the State Police Bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent as thirty states have so far approved the bill. The proposed State Police system has crossed a major constitutional hurdle, with 30 State Houses of Assembly approving the amendment required to pave the way for its establishment. This leaves six states yet to submit approved bill to the National Assembly for onward transmission to the President for subsequent assent. The six states that have not approved the bill are Kano, Cross River, Abia, Niger, Benue and Oyo. The Senate has, however, given them up till November 15 to do so, warning that failure to respond by the deadline could be deemed as withholding approval. The six states are expected to communicate their decisions before November 15, when the National Assembly intends to forward the proposed constitutional amendment to President Bola Tinubu for subsequent. Disclosing these while updating lawmakers on the progress of consultations with the 36 state legislatures on the proposed amendment yesterday, the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, said the number of approvals had exceeded the constitutionally required two-thirds of the 36 state legislatures. According to him, for the process to be rounded off, it has to be in three phases, with the National Assembly expected to pass the bill; the approval by at least two-thirds of the state legislature; and the President to sign the bill into law. He added that the National Assembly had fulfilled its responsibility by passing the bill and transmitting it to all 36 State Houses of Assembly for consideration and approval. Bamidele said: “Let me explain again, for the avoidance of doubt, three keywords are used in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, as amended. The first word is passage, the second word is approval and the third assent. “The reason the writers of our Constitution, our forefathers, put all these specific words is to ensure that no part of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria can be easily amended without the buying in of all the critical stakeholders at all levels of governance. “The passage of the bill was the responsibility of the National Assembly, and that has been completed. This came as Nigeria’s economy grew by 3.89 per cent in real terms during the quarter, driven by improved performance in the oil and non-oil sectors. Figures from the Budget Office of the Federation (BOF), contained in its 2026 Budget Performance Report, showed that the fiscal deficit was N4.69 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N7.86 trillion for the January–March period, representing N3.18 trillion below projection. The report showed that aggregate Federal Government revenue stood at N5.08 trillion, compared with the quarterly target of N9.22 trillion, resulting in a shortfall of N4.14 trillion. This represented about 55 per cent of projected revenue. Similarly, aggregate government expenditure amounted to N9.76 trillion, against the projected N17.08 trillion, indicating an underperformance of N7.32 trillion, or about 57.2 per cent of the target. On deficit financing, domestic borrowing stood at N3.9 trillion, compared with the prorated target of N4.61 trillion, leaving a shortfall of N704.03 billion. However, foreign borrowing, projected at N2.70 trillion for the quarter, recorded no actual inflow during the period. The Federal Government also realised N287.44 billion from multilateral and bilateral project-tied loans, against the quarterly target of N512.23 billion, while privatisation proceeds stood at N3.32 billion, compared with the projected N47.29 billion. The figures highlight the government’s difficulties in generating sufficient revenue and accessing planned financing sources to support budget implementation. nigeria.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
nigeria.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital. The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed. The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting. According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy. The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained. Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled. The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area. In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident. Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.” The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state. It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.” It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels. Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.” The post Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

The Brittany-based lender said in a statement that the incident was under control, that operations were resuming and that customer assets were not affected. It suspended some transactions as a precaution. “This incident has had no impact on (customer) assets and has only caused a delay in the execution of certain transfers,” the bank said on its website, in a translation published by Reuters . In a follow-up question-and-answer note , Credit Mutuel Arkea said the attackers went through the platform of one of its service providers and reached the bank directly. They used the bank’s own account to send transactions to other banks, which then potentially allowed them to convert the money into cryptocurrency through specialized platforms, the bank said. No customer accounts at its federations or subsidiaries were used, the bank said. It denied French press reports that the attackers got in through Fortuneo, its online banking arm, and said the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack was “a sophisticated attack from the outside,” not the result of human error. The size of the Credit Mutuel Arkea hack The bank has not given a final figure. entertainment.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury
entertainment.description: Ejiro Amos Tafiri , a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. entertainment.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. entertainment.description: The Goalkeepers 2026 Event in Dakar brought together innovators, global leaders and experts on how AI can be further leveraged by Africans for an equitable future On October 29, 2026, Africans gathered in Dakar, Senegal, to discuss the continent’s relationship with the world’s fastest-growing technology: artificial intelligence (AI). This event was part of the Goalkeepers 2026 series and was themed “Make This Matter: Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth .” It brought together professionals and innovators who focused on how Africa can adopt AI to fill gaps and ensure equitable access across various sectors . Africans are leveraging AI for business, education and more, but as AI continues to develop and expand rapidly, it is crucial for us to use it on a bigger scale, ensuring collective development and an equitable future for all. This makes the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar particularly significant. Nigerian influencer, Saskay, at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 The event included several activities, including performances from the legendary Youssou N’Dour , a Qui veut changer le monden session where people pitched their ideas, conversations about AI and equity and more. Here are some of the major talking points at the event: AI and Existing Solutions The event was graciously hosted in English and French by Fatou Jupiter Toure , who opened by sharing a powerful African message: “It is not about what you can do. It is about what we can do for each other.” Despite the diverse cultures and beliefs that exist on the continent, Africans have remained held by the belief of “I am because you are.” This is why, despite AI’s fast growth, Africans are coming together to examine how much it concerns them, how it can be properly leveraged and what dangers and challenges lie ahead. Fatou Jupiter Toure hosting the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar Nevertheless, Africans have done a great deal of work with AI. Innovators have used AI tools to provide solutions in their local communities. Vyonne Njeri shared how she got into healthcare and how AI has been greatly helping in the community she serves. In the Goalkeepers 2026 Report , Vyonne said she got into healthcare during a visit to see her uncle, a priest in a small, East Kenyan town called Modogashe. sports.title: New CBA proposal adjusts salary cap, floor
sports.description: ATLANTA, GA - MAY 13: A locked padlock and chain against two official MLB baseballs representing a potential lockout between Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) for the 2027 MLB season, as photographed on May 13, 2026 in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Major League Baseball has amended its salary cap and floor proposal to the MLB Players Association. Now that the 2026 season is complete and baseball is into its offseason, MLB has proposed delaying the start of the salary cap and floor to the 2028 season. The rest of their proposals would begin with the 2027 season but the teams would have a full season to make adjustments to prepare themselves for the coming changes. The owners further proposed increasing the cap to $258.2 million from the original $245.3 million and the floor to $180.2 million from $171.2 million. The new numbers reflect a 50-50 split of the projected revenue for the 2028 season. A change to the retirement proposal The offer also includes $282 million in luxury tax revenue to be given to players in cash payments instead of being placed into retirement benefits. In the present system, when a team pays luxury tax, half of the money goes into player benefits and the other half to the teams. For the 2027 season, the league is offering to pay the retirement portion directly to the players. According to league estimates , $285,000 would go to each player who received a full year of service time, $213,400 to a player with three-quarters of a year of service, $142,300 to a player with a half year of service, and $71,100 to any player with a quarter year of service. Teams outside the guidelines Per the MLB numbers, 12 teams would have to raise payroll to meet the minimum proposed floor while eight teams would have to decrease their payroll to meet the cap. Those numbers are based on current payrolls and would change based on what teams spend in 2027. Players response The MLB Players Association predictably responded negatively to the new offer. “MLB owners continue to propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values.” The statement continued, “a massive reduction in player compensation, elimination of fundamental player rights, plus a gutting of domestic and international amateur entry systems.” A statement virtually identical to the previous proposal from the owners. Sweetening the pot? This appears to be an attempt by the league to sweeten the deal for the players but doesn’t seem to have the desired effect. The baseline for the union is their unwillingness to accept a salary cap and floor as the start of negotiations. The current contract expires and 11:59 pm eastern time on Dec. 1. The owners have made it clear they intend to lock the players out if no deal is reached by that time.

sports.description: On the occasion of the International tie Day at Saint Mark's square in front of Saint Mark church on upper town, Honour Cravat Regiment changing the guard on 18 Oct 2014, Zagreb,Croatia. Here’s what you need to know about the Croatian champions! Zagreb: Croatia’s Capital With a population of around 750,000, Zagreb is Croatia’s largest city, and the use of its name dates back nearly 1000 years to 1094 AD. The city emerged from two medieval settlements (Gric and Kaptol) and began rapid development and expansion when the two combined in the 19th century. It has played a crucial role in the political history of Croatia, and in 1941 it became the capital of a Croatian puppet state controlled by the Axis powers. After being freed in 1945, Croatia became a part of Yugoslavia from the end of the Second World War until 1991. Zagreb was the centre of a newly independent Croatia during and following the Croatian War of Independence (1991-1995). On a lighter note, Zagreb is home to the world’s shortest public transport funicular, which connects the city’s old town to its newer Novi Zagreb area. It spans a total of 66m, and between its opening in 1890 to 1934, it was powered by steam. Nowadays, the journey is electrified and lasts approximately a minute. The city also keeps many of its old traditions. Every day at noon, a cannon is fired from Lotrščak Tower beside the funicular to mark midday. This has happened every day since 1877. Zagreb also has over 200 gas street lamps which are still lit manually every night, and this tradition dates back to 1863. There are also a number of weird and wonderful museums to visit in the Croatian capital. These include the Museum of Hangovers, the Museum of Laughter, the Museum of Broken Relationships, and a mushroom museum. Dinamo Zagreb: A Brief History Dinamo Zagreb were initially formed in 1911 when Croatia was a part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Upon the end of the Second World War, the club was dissolved by communist authorities; however, it was re-established just three days later on the ninth of June, 1945. The new club inherited the colours, nickname, badge and fanbase of the original club. Its name was changed to Croatia Zagreb in 1993 – a move which was seen as a political move to move away from the club’s communist past amidst Croatian independence. However, this name was never accepted by supporters, and the name Dinamo Zagreb was reinstated in the year 2000. Dinamo Zagreb is Croatia’s most successful club and has lifted the Croatian league 25 times, most recently last season, in which they finished 20 points ahead of second-placed Hajduk Split. sports.description: FBL-EUR-C1-LENS-COMO - AFP Como head coach Cesc Fabregas expressed frustration over failing to keep a clean sheet even after watching his side dismantle Lens 9-1 on Wednesday night. No Italian club had previously managed seven away goals in European Cup or Champions League history before the Serie A visitors ran riot in France. Italian visitors rewrite history books Fabregas saw his maiden Champions League away win slightly soured by a second-half consolation strike as Como recorded their sixth consecutive victory across all competitions. Having beaten RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home either side of a 3-2 loss at Feyenoord, the visitors climbed to fourth in the standings despite missing Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao, Jesus Rodriguez and Jayden Addai. Tournament top scorer Tasos Douvikas netted a treble to score in all four European outings, while Nico Paz, Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and 18-year-old debutant Matteo Papaccioli also struck. Manager urges humility after rout Speaking to Sky Sport Italia about sitting fourth midway through the league phase, Fabregas smiled: "It is also our fourth ever Champions League game, so four is the key number here. "I'm happy, this is football and everything went our way. The lads did well, now we have to prepare for a very important match on Sunday, the ninth in a run between breaks for international duty." Urging his young squad to stay grounded after their historic display, the Spaniard added: "It is a wonderful night for Como, for all our fans and many lads here who are at the start of their careers, but they need to keep their feet on the ground, be humble, keep learning and not think everything will go well from here on. "They must keep working to continue these performances." Defensive lapse frustrates former midfielder Despite almost every goal coming from slick passing moves out from the back and an early penalty against Maxence Caqueret being overturned by VAR, Como are still waiting for their first European shutout after conceding a 65th-minute corner volley. Reflecting on that solitary blemish, Fabregas confessed: "I am angry over the goal we conceded, as we changed something in our defending with the three substitutions. "Plus it was scored by a former teammate of mine, I played with Ruben Aguilar at Monaco, and I told him I'd never seen you score a goal like that before! It was honestly a great goal." Defending champions await this weekend Como must now shift their focus back to domestic duties ahead of a challenging Serie A Matchday 11 trip to reigning Scudetto holders Inter on Sunday , November 8, prior to the international break. On the continental front, the Lariani will resume their league phase campaign by hosting AEK Athens and visiting Real Betis. Fabregas' men will then wrap up their schedule against Paris Saint-Germain before travelling to Barcelona on January 27.

The analyst company expects inference to account for over 70 percent of computing demand by next year, adding that it's growing fastest at the edge. Why enterprises are building their own All this investment in AI infrastructure might once have come mainly for hyperscalers, but that's changing quickly. Adoption is spreading quickly beyond public cloud service providers into enterprise environments, IDC adds. They're eager to run agentic AI in-house. There are plenty of reasons for companies to own their own AI infrastructure rather than offloading it to the cloud. One of these is data control, especially in regulated sectors such as finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and the public sector that have sovereign data requirements. technology.title: Uranium cubes reveal why the German nuclear project failed
technology.description: During World War II, physicists on the Manhattan Project worried that the Nazi German nuclear program might achieve the first nuclear bomb before the US and its allies. That's not what transpired, but historians have debated just how close the Germans came to achieving criticality in their last attempt at building a reactor: the B8 pile. Werner Heisenberg, who led that effort, claimed that they were close and had only needed a little more uranium. But according to a paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus, that was not the case: the project simply didn't have sufficient uranium and heavy water to build a working bomb, given the design they were using. This particular research started in 2013, when University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth—a co-author on the new paper—received the gift of a mysterious heavy metal cube from a friend. He instantly recognized it as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists in their unsuccessful attempt to build a working nuclear reactor. Only 14 such cubes are known to exist today. In 2019, we reported on Koeth’s quest to track down the cube’s origins, as well as several other similar cubes that had somehow found their way across the Atlantic. At the time, Koeth and his partner in the quest, then-graduate student Miriam “Mimi” Hiebert, had tracked down ten such cubes around the US. For instance, the Smithsonian Institute had a German uranium cube in storage. They tracked a third cube to Harvard University, where it was regularly passed around to students in introductory physics classes as a curiosity. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Apple turns iCloud into spy cloud, will start looking at public share links
technology.description: If you share content using public iCloud links, Apple could soon be looking over your shoulder and checking for "harmful content." The iBiz announced plans to moderate publicly accessible iCloud share links in version 27.3 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS on a support page published on Tuesday. To clarify, this applies only to iCloud content shared via links created to be accessible to anyone, as opposed to content shared directly with other people. “Items shared using Anyone with the Link will be checked by Apple for harmful content,” Apple explained on the new help page without bothering to define what harmful content means. Based on the wording, it appears those checks will apply to all iCloud items shared using "Anyone with the Link," which Apple says it can also access. The company hasn't explained how the checks will work. The share-with-anyone option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item, Apple said, even if Advanced Data Protection , Apple's optional end-to-end encryption feature for supported iCloud data, remains enabled for the account. “If you try to upload harmful content, Apple reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete the content at any time,” the help page continues, adding that the iMaker may also block or disable accounts associated with harmful content. The company also said it reserves the right to involve law enforcement when necessary, suggesting that its undefined "harmful content" category could include child sexual abuse material (CSAM), malware, and other potentially unlawful content. Without a proper definition of what it defines as harmful, however, iCloud users are essentially left at Apple’s mercy: If it chooses to continue to bend the knee to the Trump administration, for example, content deemed objectionable by the standards of political figures could end up wiped out. Apple also hasn't explained whether human moderators, automated systems, or both will be responsible for identifying and removing so-called harmful content, or whether any decisions will be left to AI, which can easily be fooled into making a bad moderation call. The scanning of such content, as mentioned above, begins with version 27.3 of Apple’s various OSes, which were released to developers in beta on Tuesday, with a general release expected in December. Apple didn’t respond to questions for this story. ®

science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Cyprus: Island of Snakes,… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Seasonal rains had started to fill Akrotiri Salt Lake when the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 captured this image of Cyprus’s Akrotiri Peninsula on October 10, 2026. NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison The island of Cyprus began to form some 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous , with molten rock pouring from the seafloor, solidifying, and building new oceanic crust . Over time, portions of this oceanic rock were wrenched upward by tectonic forces , eventually emerging as a rugged island made of ophiolite , a type of rock with a mottled green appearance said to look like the skin of a snake. Remnants of that ancient island are still visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains . During the Miocene , considerably younger layers of chalk, limestone, marl, and other marine sedimentary rocks accumulated around the island, providing material that developed into a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift . Over time, sediment poured from rivers into the channel separating the two islands and combined with marine sediments to create deltas and eventually two land bridges, or tombolos . The joined landmass comprises the Akrotiri Peninsula , now the southernmost tip of Cyprus. The sandy edges of the peninsula were visible when Landsat 8 captured these images on October 10, 2026. Akrotiri Salt Lake , a coastal lagoon that was once an arm of the Mediterranean Sea, lies between the two tombolos. The more westerly feature, the Kouris River tombolo, formed first, developing about 50,000 years ago from river-deposited gravels and sands. The eastern tombolo extended southward from Cyprus, cutting off the Mediterranean Sea only within the past 2,000 years, according to geologists . The lake’s water levels now vary markedly with the seasons, typically filling in the late autumn and winter and drying out in the summer. The influx of winter water has historically attracted sizable overwintering flamingo populations, averaging about 4,000 birds. However, the wintering flamingo population has declined in recent years, plummeting to 30 birds in 2025, according to news reports . Flamingos have long flocked to the lake to feed on fairy shrimp , which are rich in colorful substances called carotenoids that give the birds their famously pink hue . Snakes are another of the island’s more notorious animal inhabitants. In antiquity, Cyprus was known as Ophiousa , or “ land of snakes ,” likely due to its robust population of blunt-nosed vipers . This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. The aircraft can also accommodate up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads in internal and external locations, enabling a wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next. We expect her first flight under the NASA banner within the next two years, and X-70 is just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics. This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly.” The X-70 Fractal has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds and is designed to cruise at Mach .75, reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet, and provide an operational range exceeding about 1,726 miles (1,500 nautical miles). These capabilities will enable NASA to conduct demanding flight research across a broad range of operating conditions. “For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. “It’s exciting to bring on another X-plane to accelerate and drive aeronautics research.” The X-70 joins a storied legacy of experimental aircraft that have helped establish America’s leadership in aviation. From the Bell X-1, which first broke the sound barrier in 1947, to the X-15 hypersonic research aircraft and today’s X-59 quiet supersonic demonstrator, NASA has spent decades pushing the boundaries of flight. With the X-70, NASA will expand its capacity to conduct experimental flight research, accelerate the testing of emerging technologies, and advance the next generation of American aviation. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
science.description: null On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one. The U.S. Air Force’s rail-launched Super Strypi rocket lifted off from Hawaii about 9:45 p.m. local time on Nov. 3, 2015,, roared toward the sky and failed less than a minute into the long-awaited flight. (Image credit: U.S. Air Force) Why it mattered The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets. The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission . The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year. The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads. Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support. In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice , a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

science.title: Trump declares 'American space superiority for all eternity' in election night proclamation
science.description: null President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws. "The American Declaration of Freedom in Space," describes space as the "province of all humans" and asserts that the United States will lead humanity's expansion into the cosmos. The proclamation reiterates the administration's goals with NASA's Artemis program to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually sending astronauts to Mars , but introduces no new funding, programs or policy directives. "Our Nation will lead the way in the exploration, development, use, and settlement of these new frontiers — forging an interplanetary civilization founded on the enduring and inalienable rights of freedom and individual liberty," the document says. Trump invoked America's "frontier spirit," highlighting Apollo 11 astronauts as the first people in history to walk on the moon's surface and robotic rovers exploring Mars as examples of U.S. leadership, and emphasized the country's flourishing commercial space sector helping ensure "American space superiority for all eternity." "The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity," the declaration says, and pledges that America will carry the values of faith, freedom and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization. The proclamation also highlights the success of NASA's Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon and set a record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth . The follow-up to that mission, Artemis III, is scheduled to launch next summer (2027), and will test rendezvous and docking operations between NASA's Orion spacecraft and the program's two commercial lunar landers in low Earth orbit . Artemis IV will be the program's first lunar landing mission, and is targeted for 2028. A December 2025 executive order from the President reaffirmed the goal of meeting that timeline, as well as the deployment of the initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030. Trump's declaration yesterday does not establish new NASA programs, allocate additional funding or issue instructions to federal agencies. Its sweeping language, though, does echo some of the principles in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty , which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.

science.title: NASA's Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth after failed rescue attempt
science.description: null NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100. Swift — officially known as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer — launched to Earth orbit in November 2004 on a two-year mission to study gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), the most powerful explosions in the universe . "Swift" was not an acronym but rather referred to the spacecraft's observational agility. "Swift needed to detect and locate gamma-ray bursts, communicate their position to other observatories, and then swing its telescopes around to image the burst locations before their afterglows faded out," S. Bradley Cenko, Swift's principal investigator (PI) at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, said in an Oct. 23 statement . "This typically took Swift about a minute to do." Swift didn't just observe GRBs. It also studied a variety of other cosmic bodies and phenomena, from faraway supernova explosions and feeding black holes to asteroids and comets in our own solar system. And it kept doing this long after its warranty expired — for about 20 years after, in fact. The space telescope didn't conduct its final science observation until this past Oct. 20 . (Swift underwent a name change during this stretch: In 2018, it was rechristened the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after its first PI, who died the previous year.) "Swift delivered an incredible, lasting return on investment for the nation, designed for a two-year primary mission but productive for more than 10 times as long," Shawn Domagal-Goldman, director of NASA's Astrophysics Division, said in the same Oct. 23 statement. "In that time, Swift played a major role in advancing our understanding of the changing universe and was part of a revolution in astrophysics that showed how critical rapid-response observations are to the entire community," he added. science.title: Toothbrush that emits electricity may more effectively prevent gum disease
science.description: A new and improved toothbrush could help avoid trips to the dentist Westend61/Alamy A toothbrush that generates electricity may more effectively fight harmful bacteria, while removing plaque, than existing products. The toothbrush uses special bristles that produce electricity as they bend, triggering the formation of molecules that damage bacterial membranes. When put to the test, it led to more than twice the reduction of plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding as conventional toothbrushes. “The concept is great,” says Nicholas Jakubovics at Newcastle University, UK, who wasn’t involved in the research. “Basically, the mechanical forces recharge the surface, so it’s really innovative. Anything that even slightly improves the way dental care works could have a benefit, because oral disease is just so widespread.” Read more How regrowing your own teeth could replace dentures and implants Oral diseases, such as tooth decay, affect nearly half the global population . Brushing regularly can help remove plaque, a sticky layer of bacteria that forms on teeth. These bacteria can produce acids that cause cavities and irritate gums, sometimes leading to tooth loss. Advertisement But even thorough brushing can leave behind bacteria deep in plaque or between teeth, allowing colonies to grow back within hours. Researchers have previously developed toothbrushes with antibacterial metal nanoparticles, including silver and zinc, embedded in their bristles , although their long-term effectiveness is uncertain. Others have designed ionic toothbrushes that use electric currents to help loosen plaque , but they are dependent on batteries. Now, Yanhui Lu at Peking University in China and her colleagues have turned to studies showing that so-called piezoelectric materials fight bacteria in infected wounds and medical implants. These generate electric charges under pressure , prompting Lu’s team to develop toothbrush bristles made from piezoelectric plastic. science.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
science.description: null Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead," but new spacecraft observations suggest the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping. That means that Olympus Mons , the extinct Martian volcano that at around 16 miles (26 kilometers) above the surrounding Martian plains is the largest mountain in the solar system , may in fact be a slumbering giant. The observations were made with the European Space Agency (ESA) mission ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) as it studied volcanic fissures along the Alba Mons region of the Red Planet. Alba Mons is in the Tharsis region of Mars, the same area that is home to Olympus Mons. While the latter is the tallest volcano in the solar system, at 374 miles (600 km) across, about the size of Arizona, the Alba Mons region is the largest volcano when considering surface area. TGO detected gas containing hydrogen chloride making its way to the surface of Mars through the Alba Mons fissures. The same gas is commonly found escaping from magmatic vents on Earth, with the compound coming from hot magma beneath the surface. Detecting it on Mars is a sign of dormant Martian volcanism. Orbital imagery had previously shown some volcanoes appear to have been active within the last few million years, and seismometers have detected the rumbling of "marsquakes," both implying the Red Planet is volcanically active. However, eruptions and lava flows have been conspicuous by their absence. "Our findings suggest that Mars has retained enough internal heat to support volcanic activity until recently, and possibly still does," team co-leader and scientist at the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences, Daniel Mège, said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "The TGO was able to find the smoking gun. It was like looking for a needle in a haystack." Evidence of dormant Martian volcanism is rising Mège and colleagues were first alerted to something strange happening on Mars when they noticed spikes of hydrogen chloride during Martian summer and on the northern hemisphere of the Red Planet. That is both a time and place at which hydrogen chloride shouldn't be detected. The gas usually peaks in the northern hemisphere during winter on Mars, disappearing in the summer. This variation is connected to the water and dust cycle on Mars. An exception to the rule occurs over volcanic fissures on the flanks of the Alba Mons volcano, in early summer. The TGO followed up on this by detecting fresh and narrow fissures, in some cases hundreds of feet long, in the Alba Mons region. A clear sign of volcanism. "It's truly amazing that it spotted a handful of molecules from a perhaps intermittent source, whilst moving continuously along its orbit to monitor the whole Martian atmosphere," Mège said. science.title: NASA Announces Ka-Band Satellite Relay Awards for Space Communications
science.description: Credit: NASA NASA selected three companies on Wednesday to perform work to develop Ka-band space relay capability concepts that are compatible with current missions in space, ensuring service continuity for existing spacecraft without requiring modifications to their onboard systems. Through this work, NASA will aim to acquire end-to-end solutions that include space, ground, launch, operations, and integration elements, as one of many customers in the commercial marketplace. The awards, under the Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 Broad Agency Announcement Appendix E, are firm-fixed-price contracts that give NASA the option to provide additional funding up to the award limit to advance from initial concept development and risk reduction to an in-orbit flight demonstration. The initial period of performance runs from Nov. 4 through May 3, 2027, with additional priced options to continue work through 2029. The contract awardees with maximum potential value inclusive of all future options are: Astranis Space Technologies Corp. for $264.3 million. Global Enterprise Solutions Inc. for $340.4 million. Viasat Inc. for $460.9 million. Facilitated through the agency’s SCaN (Space Communications and Navigation) program’s Communications Services Project, this work supports NASA’s decision to gradually retire the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet and adopt commercial services for future missions. In addition to the commercial capabilities currently under development by the program’s industry partners, Ka-band services are needed to support select in-orbit missions that cannot feasibly modify flight hardware or transition to non-compatible commercial services.
